deficiencies.description: The rewrite adds a link claiming that the slice through a tumour illustrates the explanting of tumours ('illustrates this'), whereas the lecturer merely states that the viewer is looking at a slice through a tumour with a stain to observe morphology.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: So the other thing to appreciate is that when, if you like, biologists are studying tumors, often they will explant the tumor. Here you're looking at a slice through a tumor and a stain to look at the morphology.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: A slice through a tumour, with a stain to show the morphology, illustrates this [FIGURE].
deficiencies.studentHarm: A student may incorrectly believe that a stained histological slice demonstrates tumour explantation, conflating histological sectioning with tissue explant culture.

considerations.sourcePassage: Cancer biologists will also, for example, disaggregate a tumor like this and try to get them to grow in culture to study the properties of these individual tumor cells.
considerations.reason: The shift from active speech to passive voice ('so that the properties of the individual tumour cells can be studied') is an allowed stylistic rewrite that preserves the original meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: Primary cells really don't grow in culture.
considerations.reason: Dropping the conversational intensifier 'really' preserves the underlying factual statement without removing a scientific hedge.

considerations.sourcePassage: Whoops, I forgot to start my clock. Okay.
considerations.reason: This is a remark to the audience and lecturer self-talk, which is explicitly allowed to be dropped.

considerations.sourcePassage: with regard to the contributions of things like the stroma and other things.
considerations.reason: Rendering 'and other things' as 'and other components' is an allowed stylistic improvement that does not add new factual content.
